Getting started
The first-run set-up checklist and quick tour.

Loading…

Paste a key and tap Save & use — Chapbook picks that provider's current model automatically. Keys are write-only (never shown again); save a new key before testing it.

About you · your voice

This guides every AI feature — drafts, the writing partner, the goblin, figures. It's a starting point, not a script: the AI captures the spirit, it won't parrot your exact words. Leave a field blank to keep the neutral default.

Connect your storage Advanced · optional

Your text and images already live in your GitHub repo — free, forever. There's nothing to set up here for normal writing. You only need this for video or large media: connect your own Cloudflare R2 bucket and clips upload straight to storage you own — no server in between, and nothing stored on anyone else's account.

  1. Create a free Cloudflare account, then an R2 bucket and an API token with Object Read & Write.
  2. Paste the endpoint, bucket name, keys and public URL into the fields below, then Save R2 keys.
  3. Add the bucket's CORS policy (the Show CORS policy button below) so your browser is allowed to upload.
Video storage — Cloudflare R2

Optional. Add your own Cloudflare R2 keys and the video block gains an Upload to R2 button — your phone uploads a clip straight to your bucket, no server in between. Keys are stored only in this browser, like your GitHub token. Create an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on the bucket.

Where the bucket serves objects publicly — your R2 custom domain, or the pub-…r2.dev URL. The video's src becomes <public base>/videos/….

Uploads go through a small Cloudflare Worker that writes to the same bucket via an R2 binding — it never touches <account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (which can fail a TLS handshake on some accounts). Deploy the Worker from the cloudflare/r2-upload-worker folder in your blog repo (the repo Chapbook created for you), then paste its URL + secret here. Access key / secret above aren't needed on this path — but keep the Public base URL set.

The same Worker also powers free image generation (✦ Generate on any image block) via Cloudflare Workers AI (FLUX) — no AI key needed. Add the [ai] binding to the Worker's wrangler.toml and redeploy (npx wrangler deploy) to enable it.

Browser uploads need a CORS policy on the bucket. Paste this at Cloudflare → R2 → your bucket → Settings → CORS policy:

Note: this is a raw upload — no transcode (the clip is stored as-is). On a UK ISP/mobile network, R2 uploads can be blocked by SNI filtering — turn on a VPN/WARP if an upload fails to connect.

Your data & this device

Your drafts, writing sessions, snapshots and ideas live only in this browser. Published posts and media are safe in your GitHub repo (and R2 bucket), but anything unpublished can be lost if this browser clears its storage. Export a backup, or move your work to another machine.

Export downloads a single JSON of every local draft. Import merges a file back in (same-id drafts are overwritten; everything else is added).

Sign out / forget this device

On a shared or borrowed computer, wipe everything Chapbook has stored here — your GitHub token, AI and R2 keys, your licence, and all local drafts — and return to the activation screen. This can't be undone, so export first if you want to keep your drafts.

Site settings

Custom domain

By default your blog lives at <you>.github.io/<repo>. Own a domain (e.g. yourname.com)? Point it here. You buy the domain from any registrar — GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, etc. — then add the records below.

Add these records at your registrar (where you bought the domain):
Type Name / Host Value

GitHub auto-provisions a free HTTPS certificate once DNS resolves (can take a few minutes to an hour the first time). Then your blog is live at .

Note: brand-new blogs created from the template serve straight at your domain's root. A blog made before this feature keeps its /<repo>/ sub-path until its deploy-pages.yml is updated to detect the CNAME file.

The look your blog is published with. Change it any time — your posts are untouched.

These power your newsletter sign-up and contact form. Grab a free endpoint from formspree.io — create a form, then copy its URL (e.g. https://formspree.io/f/abcd1234). Leave blank to hide the forms; add them any time.

        Privacy
        
    
  
        
  
        

        



        
  
        How Chapbook handles your information. Last reviewed: 15 July 2026.
        
  
        Chapbook is local-first. It runs entirely in your browser and talks directly to the services you connect it to. There is no Chapbook server sitting between you and your data.
        

  
        What stays in your browser — and only your browser
        
  
        Your GitHub token, your AI provider key(s) and your optional Cloudflare R2 keys are stored in this browser's local storage (under helm.studio.config.v1). Your drafts, writing-partner sessions, version snapshots and saved ideas are stored in this browser's IndexedDB database. None of this is ever sent to us — each key is used only to reach the service it belongs to.
        

  
        Publishing to GitHub
        
  
        When you sign in with GitHub, Chapbook requests the public_repo scope — enough to commit to your public blog repository, and nothing more. Publishing commits straight from your browser to your own GitHub repository using your token. If you use the device-flow sign-in, the login handshake is passed through a small relay so your browser can reach GitHub's login endpoints; that relay holds no secret and stores nothing.
        

  
        AI features (bring your own key)
        
  
        If you add an AI key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), AI requests go directly from your browser to that provider using your key. They do not pass through us. Your chosen provider's own privacy terms apply to those requests.
        

  
        Video and large media (optional Cloudflare R2)
        
  
        If you connect a Cloudflare R2 bucket, media uploads go straight from your browser to your own bucket (signed in your browser, or via a small upload Worker you deploy). We never receive or store your media.
        

  
        What we receive
        
  
        The only information that reaches us is what's needed to sell you a licence and let you trial the product:
        
  
          
    
        • If you buy a licence through Stripe, we receive your name and email so we can create your licence key and email it to you. The key is signed on the owner's own machine — the signing key never touches a public server.
          • 
    
        • If you request a free trial, your email address is stored in a private queue so a 7-day key can be minted and emailed to you.
          • 
    
        • Anonymous usage counts: Chapbook increments a per-day total when a licence is activated or the app is installed. These are counts only — no IP address, no licence key, no identifying information — stored in Netlify Blobs.
          • 
  
        

  
        What we do NOT collect
        
  
        We do not collect or receive your drafts, posts, media, GitHub token, AI keys, R2 keys or your author profile. We don't track your writing, we don't use tracking cookies or third-party analytics, and we never sell or share your information.
        

  
        Deleting your data
        
  
        Everything Chapbook stores locally can be wiped at any time from Settings → “Sign out / forget this device” (or by clearing this browser's site data). Your published posts and uploaded media live in your own GitHub repository and R2 bucket and stay entirely under your control. To have your sales or trial email removed from our records, email support@rqai.co.uk.
        

  
        Contact
        
  
        Questions about privacy? Email support@rqai.co.uk.
        

        


        
  
        Terms of use. Last reviewed: 15 July 2026.
        

  
        Who we are
        
  
        Chapbook is sold by RQAI Ltd, United Kingdom. Contact: support@rqai.co.uk.
        

  
        Your licence
        
  
        A Chapbook licence is a yearly subscription for one person. After purchase we email you a licence key; entering it unlocks Chapbook in your browser, on any of your own devices. The key is valid for your paid year and is non-transferable — please don't share or resell it. Your subscription renews automatically through Stripe each year, and each renewal issues you a fresh key by email. If you cancel, or a renewal payment fails, Chapbook keeps working until the end of the period you've paid for.
        

  
        Free trials
        
  
        Trial keys unlock Chapbook for 7 days, free, with no payment details taken. One trial per person.
        

  
        Your content and accounts
        
  
        You are responsible for your own GitHub, AI-provider and Cloudflare accounts and for everything you publish with them. You keep all rights to your content; Chapbook claims no ownership of it — and by design, never even receives it.
        

  
        Third-party services
        
  
        Chapbook works with GitHub, your chosen AI provider and (optionally) Cloudflare. Their terms govern your use of them, and their availability, pricing and behaviour are outside our control.
        

  
        Cancelling
        
  
        Cancel your renewal any time from your Stripe receipt email, or by emailing support@rqai.co.uk. Cancelling stops future charges; your key keeps working until your paid year ends.
        

  
        Acceptable use
        
  
        Don't use Chapbook for unlawful purposes, and don't attempt to share, resell, redistribute or circumvent the licence.
        

  
        Provided “as is”
        
  
        Chapbook is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind. To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for loss arising from its use — including loss of drafts or content — and our total liability to you is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the claim arose. Please keep your own backups (see Settings → Export drafts).
        

  
        Your statutory rights
        
  
        Nothing in these terms affects your statutory rights as a consumer.
        

  
        Changes
        
  
        We may update these terms; material changes will be reflected here with a new “last reviewed” date.
        

  
        Governing law
        
  
        These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.
        

  
        Contact
        
  
        Questions? Email support@rqai.co.uk.
        

        


        
  
        Refund policy. Last reviewed: 15 July 2026.
        

  
        We want you to be happy with Chapbook. If it isn't right for you, email support@rqai.co.uk within 14 days of your purchase for a full refund — no questions asked. The same applies to a renewal charge: if you didn't mean to renew, email us within 14 days of the charge.
        

  
        What happens on a refund
        
  
        Your licence key is revoked and Chapbook stops unlocking on your devices. Anything you've already published to your own GitHub repository or R2 bucket stays yours and is unaffected.
        

  
        How the money comes back
        
  
        Refunds go to your original payment method through Stripe, and typically appear within 5–10 working days.
        

  
        After 14 days
        
  
        We don't offer partial refunds mid-year, but you can cancel any time to stop future renewals — and if something's broken, email us first: we'd rather fix it.
        

  
        Free trials
        
  
        Free trials are free — there's nothing to refund.
        

  
        How to request one
        
  
        Email support@rqai.co.uk from, or quoting, the email address you purchased with.
